authorityClaim: This artifact PROPOSES the DR-124 state-class/owner/writer design contract: the four-class matrix file 04 states, preview scope, placement of named durable bytes including the previously unassigned grant journal, required manifest declaration fields, and the four negative-test classes. It applies nothing, does not design authoritative-evidence recipes, does not invent a purge/D9 code, and does not authorize docs/v2/implementation/. The DR-124 row remains OPEN until coordinator disposition after independent review.
purpose: Give DR-124 a T2-02 candidate that extracts the four-class table, scopes preview honestly, and assigns or expressly reserves every named durable byte the preview writes or a sibling contract routes here. Grant-journal placement is a proposed supersession of P-005-2, not a silent assignment.

registerRowQuoted.rowVerbatim: | DR-124 | Closed state-class/owner/writer architecture | Semantic/evidence/storage/lifecycle owners | [State classes](04-lifecycle-delivery-and-operations.md#state-classes-and-authority) | Matrix for authoritative evidence, analysis-affecting durable state, rebuildable cache/index, operational metadata; Plan/Run, custody/backup/purge/migration rules and cross-class negative tests | OPEN | Hard blocker for stateful component blueprint |

linesVerbatim: | State class | Owner / sole writer | Plan/Run consequence | Custody, purge, migration, and test rule |

| Authoritative evidence | Semantic host through host-owned commit; storage is mechanics | Sealed Run/evidence only through accepted recipes | Durable custody, backup/restore disclosure, retention/tombstone/purge authority, atomic migration and recovery; no component writer |

| Analysis-affecting durable state | Owning host semantic surface under strict config/lock | Enters Plan/Run identity only where the applied contract requires | Versioned/migrated under host authority; mutation and rollback cannot rewrite history |

| Rebuildable cache/index | Declared host or component mechanic under a host namespace | Never changes semantic result; a cache hit equals recomputation | May be discarded/rebuilt; provenance and corruption tests prove no authority or hidden input |

| Operational metadata | Core lifecycle/audit/doctor owner | Excluded from Plan/Run unless an applied owner explicitly promotes a field | Journaled/redacted/bounded; backup/purge scope disclosed; never a peer evidence writer |
Every component manifest declares its state class, owner, writer, schema,
migration, retention, backup, purge, and recovery contract. Cross-class writes,
cache-to-authority promotion, undeclared Plan inputs, and component evidence
commits are negative tests under DR-124 and DR-G19.

lifecycle.standing: DESIGN-ANSWERED for the carrier and the named branches below. Authoritative purge semantics remain DR-113. Permission/generation identity remains DR-105. This artifact does not mint purge/D9 codes.
lifecycle.carrier: One durable journal per (project, grant generation), matching permission-truth-tables.v6. Operation identity is carried on records. The next sequence number is derived solely from the durable journal tail of that carrier.
lifecycle.retention: Sequence records are retained for the life of the grant generation. There is no drop bound. Archival is append-forward copy, not truncation.
lifecycle.operationPurge: MUST NOT terminalize the shared (project, grant generation) journal. MAY append an operation-scoped closure record naming that operation. Further appends for other operations on the same generation remain lawful. Authoritative purge of operation-owned non-journal bytes remains DR-113.
lifecycle.projectPurge: MUST NOT drop grant-journal sequence. On a healthy open carrier, this event is one of the two FIRST-wins terminalizers under terminalization.openHealthy. On an already-TERMINAL or failClosedNoAppend carrier it is a no-op. Authoritative project purge of non-journal bytes remains DR-113.
lifecycle.grantGenerationClosure: On a healthy open carrier, this event is the other FIRST-wins terminalizer under terminalization.openHealthy. A new grant generation, if any, is a new carrier. Sequence restarts at that carrier's origin. MUST NOT continue the closed generation's carrier.
lifecycle.backupRestore: Included in SC-OPS backup/restore of the host-owned operational namespace. Restore MUST replay order and MUST NOT invent or drop sequence records. If the restored tail may have lost later durable sequence (no completeness/high-water witness), that grant generation is permanently revoked (failClosedNoAppend). Continuation is only a new grant generation, which MUST NOT continue the closed carrier. The closed generation's (project, grant generation, sequence) triples are never reused. This artifact does not mint the witness class; absence of a witness is fail-closed. Witnessless restore MUST write carrierQuarantineRecord and MUST NOT append to the restored journal and MUST NOT promote it. The durable revoked standing is that external record, not a word in this artifact.
lifecycle.migration: Forward-only append of a migration marker plus continued sequence on the same generation. Historical records are not rewritten.
lifecycle.lossOrCapacity: SPLIT. Temporary capacity with an intact proven tail is capacityPause and is NOT failClosedNoAppend. Permanent uncertain-tail loss is uncertainTailLoss and IS failClosedNoAppend via the external carrierQuarantineRecord. MUST NOT drop or compact away order to make room in either branch.
lifecycle.reversibility: Overturn of SUP-124-GRANT-JOURNAL restores the three prohibitions for NEW writes. Already-written candidate records stay grant-journal bytes under standing FROZEN-UNDER-OVERTURN: not rewritten, not dropped, not compacted, no new appends. Migration of those frozen bytes requires a separately authorized, owner-concurred recording and a user-express D-096 (A) grant. This artifact does not perform that migration.
lifecycle.grantJournalTerminalMarkerIsNot: The binding retention policy and tombstones bytes reserved elsewhere in bytePlacement. The marker is a grant-journal sequence record.

terminalization.terminalIs: A property of the (project, grant generation) carrier, not of an event.
terminalization.openHealthy: On a healthy open carrier (no capacityPause, no carrierQuarantineRecord, not FROZEN-UNDER-OVERTURN), the FIRST of {projectPurge, grantGenerationClosure} MUST append exactly one grant-journal-terminal-marker and atomically set the carrier TERMINAL. Healthy TERMINAL is derived solely from that journal marker. Any later projectPurge or grantGenerationClosure on an already-TERMINAL carrier is a no-op and MUST NOT append a second marker.
terminalization.capacityPauseIsNotFailClosedNoAppend: capacityPause is not a failClosedNoAppend state. See lifecycle.capacityPause. A terminalizer that arrives during the pause is stored as pendingTerminalizerRecord, not swallowed.
terminalization.failClosedNoAppend: uncertainTailLoss (carrierQuarantineRecord present), witnessless-restore revocation (same carrierQuarantineRecord), and FROZEN-UNDER-OVERTURN are non-appending terminal-equivalent states. Purge or generation-closure on those carriers is a non-appending branch: observe the existing fail-closed/frozen standing and perform no journal append. Healthy TERMINAL is never inferred from these states; it exists only when the journal carries the terminal marker.
terminalization.frozenUnderOverturnSource: FROZEN-UNDER-OVERTURN is derived from the applied coordinator overturn recording of SUP-124-GRANT-JOURNAL (the C-D that overturns that named supersession). It is not stored as a grant-journal append and is not carrierQuarantineRecord.
terminalization.operationPurgeNeverTerminalizes: Unchanged: operation purge MUST NOT terminalize the shared carrier.

lifecycle.sequenceIdentity: The unique order key is the triple (project, grant generation, sequence). Numeric sequence restarts at the origin of each new carrier. Non-reuse applies only within a carrier. A new grant generation MUST NOT continue the closed generation's carrier; it MAY restart numeric sequence at its own origin. The closed generation's triple is never reused.
lifecycle.capacityPause: When the writer cannot append ordinary records because of a capacity boundary AND the durable tail is proven intact (no completeness/high-water doubt), the writer pauses the same carrier. This pause is temporary and is not terminal-equivalent. The journal MUST keep reserved capacity for exactly one grant-journal-terminal-marker. Ordinary appends remain refused until capacity returns. A projectPurge or grantGenerationClosure that arrives during the pause is accepted ONLY if that reserved terminal-marker is durably appended (FIRST-wins; order is the journal). If the reserved append cannot be completed, the terminalizer is a retryable refusal and is NOT a member of the FIRST-wins set. There is no external pending-terminalizer record and no second ordering authority. Recovery never treats the absence of an external record as permission to resume after an accepted terminalizer. When capacity returns and no terminal marker is present, ordinary appends resume on the same carrier.
lifecycle.uncertainTailLoss: When the durable tail is not proven intact (storage loss without a completeness/high-water witness, or any loss that makes later durable sequence uncertain), this carrier is permanently quarantined. The writer MUST persist carrierQuarantineRecord keyed by (project, grant generation) and MUST NOT append to the journal. Continuation is only a new grant generation on a new carrier. The closed generation's (project, grant generation, sequence) triples are never reused.

lifecycle.standing: DESIGN-ANSWERED. This is the durable per-carrier fact for uncertainTailLoss and witnessless-restore revocation.
lifecycle.carrier: One record per (project, grant generation), stored outside that generation's grant journal. MUST NOT be written into the journal.
lifecycle.retention: Retained for the life of the grant generation plus the quarantine. Archival is copy, not truncation.
lifecycle.writeRule: Written exactly when witnessless restore is detected or uncertainTailLoss is recognized. Write failure is fail-closed: the writer MUST NOT promote the journal.
lifecycle.recovery: Before any grant-journal append or promotion, the writer MUST consult this record. Presence means refuse promotion and refuse appends.
lifecycle.projectPurge: MUST NOT delete this record. The journal remains unpromoted; purge of non-journal bytes remains DR-113.
lifecycle.grantGenerationClosure: Non-appending on the quarantined journal. The record remains. A new generation is a new carrier and a new (absent) quarantine record.
lifecycle.backupRestore: Restored with the operational namespace. A restore that cannot prove the quarantine record's completeness MUST re-create the record rather than promote the journal.
lifecycle.migration: Forward-only copy of the record. Not rewritten in place.
lifecycle.reversibility: Clearing this record requires a separately authorized, owner-concurred recording and a user-express D-096 (A) grant. This artifact does not perform that clearing. This artifact does not mint a D-096 (A) grant.
lifecycle.journaled: The durable write (or crash-atomic clear) of this single current record is the audit. It does not linearize grant-journal sequence.
lifecycle.bound: One current record per (project, grant generation). Finite. Not an unbounded sequence.

proposedSupersession.standing: PROPOSED. This candidate does not self-apply the supersession. Neither this candidate, an independent review, nor coordinator recording by itself supplies owner concurrence. Application requires a separately authorized, reviewed recording AND a user-express D-096 (A) grant covering every named role, including the V1 coordinator. D-096 (A) is unsatisfied as of D-100. This artifact does not mint that grant. Overturn restores the P-002-4 / P-005-2 bars and the SC-OPS journaled/redacted/bounded class rule for NEW grant-journal writes. Already-written candidate records remain grant-journal bytes under FROZEN-UNDER-OVERTURN until a separately authorized owner-concurred migration; they are not silently rewritten or dropped.
proposedSupersession.whatIsSuperseded: Three displacements only, and only for DR-105 grant-journal bytes: (1) the prohibition on SC-OPS containing the DR-105 grant journal; (2) the matching P-002-4 containment prohibition; (3) the SC-OPS 'journaled/redacted/bounded' class rule as it appears in file 04, P-005-2, and P-002-4, to the extent it would require dropping or bounding away grant-journal sequence records. P-005-2 remains in force for doctor's own audit record, non-authority, non-rebuildability, and never-a-peer-evidence-writer. P-002-4 remains in force for exclusion from Plan/Run unless an applied owner explicitly promotes a field, Not rebuildable, rebuildability stays on P-002-3's cache/index class only, and the completeness obligation that DR-124 remains OPEN and must assign every persisted byte one class, owner, writer, and lifecycle before blueprint work.
proposedSupersession.whyNotSilent: v1 assigned the journal to SC-OPS without citing D-060. v2 cited D-060/P-005-2 but omitted P-002-4. v3 added P-002-4 to 'of'. v4 stated P-002-4's surviving force and added the V1 coordinator. v5 named the file 04 custody cell. v6 extended the displacement to the P-005-2 and P-002-4 instances, restored all three on overturn, and added the grant-journal lifecycle. v7 separates operation/project/generation purge, makes terminalization mandatory at grant-generation closure, revokes a restored generation after possible tail loss, and grandfathers already-written bytes under FROZEN-UNDER-OVERTURN. v8 named FIRST-wins carrier terminalization, non-appending failClosedNoAppend branches, and the (project, grant generation, sequence) key. v9 splits temporary capacityPause (intact proven tail; pendingTerminalizerRecord) from permanent uncertainTailLoss/witnessless-restore (carrierQuarantineRecord, non-append); healthy TERMINAL derives solely from the journal terminal marker; FROZEN-UNDER-OVERTURN derives from the applied coordinator overturn recording of SUP-124-GRANT-JOURNAL. v10 removes pendingTerminalizerRecord. Capacity-pause FIRST-wins is the reserved grant-journal terminal-marker slot; a failed reserved append is a retryable refusal, not an accepted terminalizer. carrierQuarantineRecord remains a single-current standing record (bound = one per carrier), not a second ordering authority.
proposedSupersession.boundednessExceptionOwner: The complete concurrence set already listed in ownersWhoseConcurrenceIsRequired, including D-060 operability. This names concurrence for the boundedness displacement. It does not mint D-096 (A).
